tasks_completed.description: Changed runtime recovery watcher semantics so stable low-count states abort fast-detect instead of restoring from historical peak counts.
tasks_completed.changes: Runtime count drops preserve the existing desired snapshot, stable fast-detect aborts, and restore-in-progress lock state suppresses fast-detect.
tasks_completed.rationale: Root cause was watcher logic treating stable low counts and peak snapshots as restore-worthy runtime desired state.

tasks_completed.description: Restricted peak snapshot usage to explicit disaster mode and added durable recovery tombstone support.
tasks_completed.changes: Restore uses session_dirs.txt by default; peak snapshots are only used when HAPPY_RECOVERY_DISASTER_MODE=1 and session_dirs.txt is empty. Added per-home session_recovery_tombstones.tsv support plus tombstone/untombstone commands and restore filtering.
tasks_completed.rationale: Prevents runtime peak deltas and manual stop/archive debt from resurrecting sessions.

tasks_completed.description: Made recovery reporting truthful for external spawns.
tasks_completed.changes: Restore logs and counters now report external_restored and daemon_tracked_restored=0; manual recover output says daemon-tracked restore is not claimed.
tasks_completed.rationale: Evidence showed externally spawned processes are often PPID=1 and not part of daemon pidToTrackedSession snapshots.

tasks_completed.description: Hardened emergency memory guard target selection and action semantics.
tasks_completed.changes: Daemon-child candidates now prefer safe process-group termination when the group does not include daemon main process groups, while transient session cgroups remain stop-unit targets. Audit JSON includes pgid/action details.
tasks_completed.rationale: OOM protection must target runaway session/process-group work instead of coarse daemon limits.

tasks_completed.description: Protected the emergency guard unit enough to run under pressure without adding daemon MemoryMax caps.
tasks_completed.changes: Added OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, Nice=-10, and best-effort I/O priority to the guard service only.
tasks_completed.rationale: The guard needs a better chance to execute during pressure, while the whole happy daemon must not receive a coarse memory cap.

blast_radius.impact: high operational impact; QA should use static checks and dry-run paths only unless user authorizes live recovery actions
host-pressure guard path; dry-run verification performed

git_rationale.root_cause_commit: N/A - operational recovery debt documented in docs/dev/context-20260523-235421.json
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: Recovery logic mixed runtime desired state with peak historical snapshots, external recovery spawned processes outside daemon tracking, and emergency guard actions lacked explicit process-group semantics.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: Runtime watcher no longer restores stable losses from peaks, restore exposes explicit disaster/tombstone/external-spawn semantics, and OOM guard targets session units or safe process groups.
